tool.name: Raw file header
tool.command: #import re ## The element identifier keeps the file's original name and extension. #set $raw_name = re.sub(r'[^\w.\-]', '_', str($raw.element_identifier)) ln -s '$raw' '$raw_name' && python '$__tool_directory__/raw_header.py' '$raw_name' --name '$raw_name' --header '$header'

param.name: raw
param.label: Raw file
param.help: A raw file of a format gwyddionpy reads (e.g. Nanonis .sxm, RHK .sm4, Bruker .spm), or any file with a text header.

has_json_property_with_value.value: "This is not a Nanonis SXM file."

tool.help:
**What it does**
Writes the header (metadata) of a raw file as JSON, for the ELN tools. The header is read with [gwyddionpy](https://github.com/FAIRmat-NFDI/gwyddionPy), which reads many scanning probe microscopy formats, also binary ones such as RHK `.sm4`.
If gwyddionpy cannot read the file, or finds no metadata, the header is the file's leading text: the text before the first binary byte or data marker (`[DATA]` of Nanonis `.dat` files), at most 64 kB.
-----
**Output**
A JSON file with `file` (the raw file's name) and `read_with` (how the header was read), then:
- **gwyddionpy:** `source_format`, `meta` (the metadata all channels share) and `channels` (per channel its name, size, units, shape and its own `meta`). A value with a unit is written as `{"value": 2.1, "unit": "V"}`. This is gwyddionpy's [JSON export](https://github.com/FAIRmat-NFDI/gwyddionPy/blob/main/docs/user/usage.md), with the shared metadata written once. No pixel data. - **leading text:** `text`, the file's own header lines.
